subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Six Types of Tea
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Six Types of Tea.

hook.text: Tea experts classify all true tea into six types based on processing: white, green, yellow, oolong, black, dark.

buildup.text: White is barely processed. Green is heated early. Yellow is lightly fermented under a damp cloth.

discovery.text: Oolong is partially oxidized (15–85%). Black is fully oxidized. Dark tea (like pu-erh) is microbially aged.

twist.text: Yellow tea is the rarest. The extra step of 'smothering' creates a smooth, mellow flavor few people ever taste.

climax.text: Each type contains thousands of individual teas—varieties within varieties, shaped by region and technique.

punchline.text: Six types, thousands of teas. One plant did all that.

quiz.question: What makes pu-erh different from other tea types?

details.summary: Tea is classified into six types based on processing: green, white, yellow, oolong, black, and dark. The key variable is oxidation, ranging from minimal in white and green to full in black. Each type has a distinct flavor profile, appearance, and cultural tradition.
details.whyItMatters: The six-type framework is the foundation of tea literacy. Understanding it helps you navigate tea menus, shops, and traditions with confidence.
takeaways: Six types: green, white, yellow, oolong, black, and dark tea
Oxidation level is the main differentiating factor
Each type spans a wide range of flavors and styles

faq.question: What is the difference between dark tea and black tea?
faq.answer: Black tea is fully oxidized, while dark tea like pu-erh undergoes microbial fermentation after processing. In Chinese, black tea is called red tea. The confusion arises from Western naming conventions that do not distinguish between oxidation and fermentation.

faq.question: Which tea type has the most caffeine?
faq.answer: Caffeine content depends more on specific leaf, brewing temperature, and steep time than tea type. However, black and pu-erh teas generally have more caffeine per cup than green or white teas because they are brewed at higher temperatures that extract more caffeine.
